ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$8.37 to the rider (voucher per NS-7) as the metered overcharge for the 5.94 km unexempt detour; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file; no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute).
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI, so the meter applies and detour km feed the fare directly (RD-2). Fare rate check: $39.42 ÷ 27.96 km = $1.410/km; meter ran 27.96 km vs the 21.469 km quoted/optimal route = 6.49 km excess, consistent with the rider's "21 km vs 28 km".

GPS trace (30 s thinned) vs quoted polyline: from pickup the trace follows the quoted corridor up to the ECP turnoff (1.2939,103.8639 ≈ 22:50:25). At 22:56:25–22:57:55 the trace runs east along the ECP (1.2970,103.8969 → 1.3052,103.8962) while the quoted route had already bent north-east inland (1.2980,103.8996 → 1.3032,103.9162); the trace then wanders north (1.3052,103.8962 / 1.3035,103.8971 / 1.3024,103.8986) into the Tampines corridor, rejoining the quoted route near 1.3158,103.9438 at ~23:10:55, then reverses direction at 23:12:25–23:14:25 (1.3179,103.9491 → 1.3167,103.9463 → 1.3158,103.9438 → 1.3149,103.9408 → 1.3123,103.9406) — a genuine out-and-back loop off the optimal route. From ~23:14:55 it follows the quoted polyline through Airport Boulevard to T3.

Detour magnitude: optimal sub-path 1.29394,103.86394 → 1.31236,103.95178 ≈ 9.94 km; driven sub-path along the trace ≈ 15.88 km; excess ≈ 5.94 km (5.94 × $1.410 = $8.37). This approximates the cited fare excess of 6.49 km.

No exemption applies. Traffic: both LTA speed-band records are band 4 on the quoted route (below the band-2 threshold) and there are no LTA incidents, so RD-4(a)/(b) do not exempt the segment — the driver's "the GPS rerouted me" claim is rejected. Consent: the chat log is empty, so there is no rider message before the detour agreeing to it (RD-5); the driver's statement alone is not consent (G11). No rider-named stop (RD-3) and no app route change is recorded. The entire loop is therefore an unexempt detour (RD-1) and the metered overcharge is refundable (RD-2).

Amount: 5.94 km × $1.410/km = $8.37 (only distance units; no waiting-time refund — metered waiting $0.02 is per RD-3(c)/RD-2, and a $0.02 add-on is de minimis). No ERP/toll overcharge (tolls $0.00). Roadside is full except the GPS hole 23:07:55–23:08:25 (30 s t-thinned spacing ≈ 60 s > 2 min? no — the actual gap is within normal sampling, so no break); dropoff GPS coincides with the dropoff point and time, so the evidence is sufficient. No flag: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute, and route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0.

Safety screen: no threats, harassment or dangerous-driving allegations in the empty chat, the complaint or the driver statement — no safety concern.

segment_findings.reason: Out-and-back loop off the ECP/Tampines corridor (~5.94 km excess, KPE-side looping near 1.312–1.318, 103.940–103.951, ~22:56–23:14). No rider message exists before the detour (chat empty) and the driver's statement is not consent (RD-5, G11); no LTA incident or band-1/2 speed band on the replaced optimal segment (RD-4); no rider-named stop (RD-3). Unexempt detour -> RD-2 refund of distance units.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's claim that 'the GPS rerouted me' is unsupported: LTA speed bands on the optimal route are band 4 (not band 1/2) and there are no incidents in the window, so RD-4 'reasonable cause' is not made out; the recorded trace shows an off-route loop back-tracking on itself (no GPS chosen alternative would do this).
Only the unexempt detour distance is refundable (5.94 km = $8.37); the remaining meter-vs-quote gap (0.55 km) is not attributable to an identified off-route segment and is not refundable under RD-2.
